label: next7_v3_fact_audit

scope.candidate_first_rule: candidate-facing-v3.json was read and solved before writer-v3.json or its editorial key was opened
scope.blind_key_comparison: All eight independently selected options match the private editorial key. This is evidence of answer agreement, not publication approval.

source_access_summary.important_limit: Unavailable here describes this actual retrieval attempt (HTTP/tool failure or inaccessible URL); it does not certify that a URL is a dead link.
source_access_summary.ledger_status: incomplete: the three Grammy URLs were all inaccessible through the actual retrieval tool, and five other original URLs also failed or were inaccessible. Suitable alternatives are recorded per item where opened.

corpus_duplicate_check.result: No exact duplicate among the eight new stems. music-people-028 has a material partial knowledge-point overlap with existing music-people-005: both centre Dolly Parton and I Will Always Love You; the new question adds Jolene and asks authorship, so it is not an exact duplicate but needs editorial replacement or a distinct song pair.

The role, Su Li-zhen/Maggie Cheung, spouses' infidelity and Angkor Wat secret claims are supported by the opened BFI pages; the remaining stylistic description should be kept clearly interpretive.

items.key_check: Celia Cruz is uniquely correct. The alternatives are notable Latin singers but do not answer the Sonora Matancera lead-singer clue.
items.finding: Both cited Smithsonian URLs failed actual retrieval (one 500, one 404), so the article cannot continue to state that Smithsonian directly supports its claims on this audit evidence. An opened Rock Hall profile directly supports the core fact: Cruz became Sonora Matancera's lead singer and remained so for fifteen years. The source list must be repaired; the claims about her later solo career are supportable but should use an opened source.

items.key_check: Dionne Warwick is uniquely correct. Rock Hall explicitly joins her to Bacharach-David and lists Walk On By; the other singers do not create a defensible competing answer.

The cited Grammy URL was inaccessible; because the article invokes it for institutional context, either replace it with an actually opened authoritative source or remove that claim.

items.key_check: Dolly Parton is uniquely correct; all alternatives are country singers but none wrote both named songs.
items.finding: Both original URLs were inaccessible, including the Grammy URL. An opened Library of Congress Magazine page is a suitable authoritative alternative and directly says Parton wrote both Jolene and I Will Always Love You; an opened Library of Congress Copyright Office post independently establishes her authorship of I Will Always Love You. The source list needs replacement. This also partially overlaps existing music-people-005, which already tests Parton and I Will Always Love You.
